newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - March cocoa gains interest, coffee stable.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - March cocoa gains interest, coffee stable.

text.p: Volatilities in the coffee options were stable this week but traders said on Thursday that values could come under downward pressure if the trend in futures stayed static.
Cocoa options saw an uneventful December expiry on Wednesday and interest is now shifted to the second-month March positions.
"It was a very peaceful expiry. Nothing happened," said one market maker.
December's lowest strike which had an open interest was 900 stg puts but the futures market was trading at around 870 stg two days before the expiry.
Open interest for the 900 puts was 140-150 lots.
"As such it had no impact on prices," said one.
March options garnered some activity early in the week in what looked to be short-covering on 900 stg puts.
The implied volatility rose slightly to 16 percent having traded on Friday for the same strike at 14.5 percent.
"Sellers appeared to be expressing a view on price direction," UK trade house Sucden said in daily commentary.

A strong New York rally this week helped London cocoa futures burst out of their rigid downtrend, but the market soon met resistance as sterling's new gains in exchange markets bolstered origin selling.
The market is underpinned by technicals, but supply and demand fundamentals remain bleak, traders said.
Attentions are focused on Ivorian arrivals this month, which may confirm earlier predictions by crop forecasters of a main crop of 900,000 tonnes.
Coffee options saw brisk trade on Wednesday and last Friday with a daily turnover of over 1,000 lots.
Wednesday's trade saw keen interest spanning over four contract months -- January, March, May and July.
This was also the first ever trading in July options, where the $1,100 puts was traded at about 33-34 percent volatility, which traders say, was quite out-of-the-money put.
June and July are the winter months in top grower Brazil, which in 1994 was hit by crop-damaging frosts that sent world prices spiralling.
Meanwhile, the traded March and May calls and puts were mainly crosses by one trade house.
January and March volatilities were fairly stable.
But traders said the premiums could come under slight selling pressure with the futures market seemed to be clinging on to its immediate range.
Robusta coffee had been kept in the narrow $1,415-$1,476 a tonne range basis January in view of little fresh fundamental inputs.

The market's upside remained capped by Asian and African selling but onn the downside, the potential was limited by scale-down industry buying. "That's probably one reason why Jan and March are under a little bit of pressure," said one.
Recommended strategies included a strangle, he said. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
